prompt_en: Photographic study of visible garment fit, showing a woman in a concrete clothing-fit situation. Use the attached image as visual guidance for her face and dark bob with wispy bangs. In the sheltered alcove of a working harbor, a brief midday pause in the rain gives her time to finish checking the field repair case on a waist-high wooden bench. Its raised metal lid carries fresh water beads, and tools lie in the open compartments. Dock rope on the bench and wet paving beyond the workshop connect the close task to the waiting boats. She leans a little toward the case with an inviting, lightly amused glance at the photographer. Her clothes remain a charcoal cotton-jersey T-shirt, an olive woven utility vest and a broad blue crinkled-nylon rain jacket. The close inner shirt, firmer vest and roomy shell retain separate textile boundaries. The blue jacket has generous shoulder width, wide sleeves and a broad hanging torso with clearance around the vest; the cuff closes at the near wrist. Its camera-near open panel and lining are folded fully behind the near shoulder and hip. A broad strip of olive rear-panel fabric is now exposed beside the olive front-panel edge, from the lower ribs to the waist. Light falls directly across that rear strip, its rectangular fabric attachment patches and their box stitching. The olive vest's two side webbing bridges each have a clearly exposed front fabric anchor and a clearly exposed rear fabric anchor, with two black woven sections joined by a central rectangular buckle on the same vest. A garment strap bridges two visible fabric anchors on the same item. At each vest side bridge, a buckle joins its two webbing sections. The upper bridge sits under the ribs and the lower bridge sits above the hip. Each rear box-stitched olive attachment patch lies on the exposed rear-panel strip; each front patch lies on the visible front-panel edge. The two buckles and the whole black paths between those paired patches are separately readable. The olive vest's front zipper joins its lower front up to the sternum, with an upper V revealing the charcoal shirt. The woman adjusts the olive vest's two side webbing bridges by gripping the lower bridge's free tail below its buckle with the near thumb and index finger while the same vest stays worn on her torso. Her near elbow stays gently outward and her other palm supports the mild forward lean beside the case. Her hips and planted legs support the standing posture. Keep the top-of-head to mid-thigh environmental crop, with the open kit beside her. A slightly more lateral near-side front three-quarter camera direction at chest height makes both exposed fabric-anchor pairs visible while her face stays readable. Soft overcast daylight belongs to the wet harbor and illuminates her face and the three clothing layers together; moderate depth of field, natural skin texture and restrained documentary fashion rendering hold the practical gesture and warm presence in one coherent moment.
